title: LRU cache
summary: A fixed-size cache that evicts the entry nobody has used for the longest time.
prompt: A lookup service keeps the most recently used results in memory. Write a class
`LruCache<TKey, TValue>` (with `where TKey : notnull`) that holds at most `capacity` entries:
cache.TryGet("a", out var a);   // true, a == 1 (and "a" is now the most recently used)
cache.Put("c", 3);              // full: evicts "b", the least recently used
- `LruCache(int capacity)`: throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when `capacity` is less than 1.
- `bool TryGet(TKey key, out TValue value)`: a hit counts as a **use**.
- `void Put(TKey key, TValue value)`: adds or **updates**; updating an existing key also counts as a use and never grows the cache.
- `int Count`: the number of entries held.
When a `Put` of a new key would go over capacity, evict the least recently used entry first.
starter: class LruCache<TKey, TValue> where TKey : notnull
public bool TryGet(TKey key, out TValue value)
public void Put(TKey key, TValue value) { }
solution: class LruCache<TKey, TValue> where TKey : notnull
readonly Dictionary<TKey, LinkedListNode<(TKey Key, TValue Value)>> map = new();
readonly LinkedList<(TKey Key, TValue Value)> order = new();   // most recent first
public bool TryGet(TKey key, out TValue value)
public void Put(TKey key, TValue value)
template: Dojo.Check("TryGet finds a stored value", dojoC.TryGet("a", out var dojoA) && dojoA == 1, "TryGet(\"a\") should return true with 1");
Dojo.Check("TryGet misses an unknown key", !dojoC.TryGet("zzz", out _), "TryGet(\"zzz\") should return false");
Dojo.Check("evicts the least recently USED key (b), not the oldest inserted (a)", !dojoC.TryGet("b", out _) && dojoC.TryGet("a", out _), "a was read after b was stored, so b should go");
Dojo.Check("keeps the newest key", dojoC.TryGet("c", out var dojoCv) && dojoCv == 3, "c should be there");
Dojo.Eq("updating does not grow the cache", 2, dojoD.Count);
Dojo.Check("updating counts as a use, so y is evicted", !dojoD.TryGet("y", out _), "y should have been evicted");
Dojo.Check("the updated value is returned", dojoD.TryGet("x", out var dojoX) && dojoX == 10, "x should be 10");
Dojo.Check("updating a key never evicts another key", dojoF.TryGet("x", out _) && dojoF.TryGet("y", out var dojoY) && dojoY == 20, "both x and y=20 should still be cached");
Dojo.Check("only the last key survives", !dojoE.TryGet(1, out _) && dojoE.TryGet(2, out var dojoTwo) && dojoTwo == "two", "");
wrong: class LruCache<TKey, TValue> where TKey : notnull
public bool TryGet(TKey key, out TValue value) => map.TryGetValue(key, out value!);
public void Put(TKey key, TValue value)
class LruCache<TKey, TValue> where TKey : notnull
readonly List<(TKey Key, TValue Value)> items = new();
public bool TryGet(TKey key, out TValue value)
public void Put(TKey key, TValue value)
hints: You need two things at once: find an entry by key quickly, and know which entry is the oldest *use*.
A `Dictionary` from key to a `LinkedListNode` gives you both: move a node to the front on every use, evict from the back.
In `Put`, remove an existing node for the key before adding the new one, so an update never counts as a second entry.
